facts.statement: The genus name Plesiopharos means "close lighthouse" because the holotype was discovered near a lighthouse in São Pedro de Moel.
facts.quote: Plesiopharos (derived from the Greek words πλησίος (plesios), "close" and φάρος (pharos), "lighthouse", because its holotype was found in the vicinity of a lighthouse + [from São Pedro de] Moel)

facts.statement: When described in 2021, Plesiopharos was the most complete and oldest known plesiosaur from the Iberian Peninsula.
facts.quote: At the time of its publication (2021), this plesiosaur was the most complete and oldest known from the Iberian Peninsula.

facts.statement: Fossils of Plesiopharos were found by collectors António Silva and Vítor Teixeira and donated to the Lourinhã Museum in 2017.
facts.quote: The fossils were found by two collectors, António Silva (1999) and Vítor Teixeira (2012) who donated them to the Lourinhã Museum in 2017

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes bones from the arm, leg, pelvic girdle, thorax, and neck.
facts.quote: The Plesiopharos holotype (ML 2302) consists of parts of the fin of the arm (humerus and radius), of the right leg (femur), pelvic girdle (pubis, ilium and ischium) of the thorax (vertebrae, ribs and gastralia) and of the neck (cervical vertebra).

facts.statement: The holotype represents an adult animal estimated to be between 2.5 and 2.8 meters in size.
facts.quote: It would be an adult animal with an estimated size between 2.5 and 2.8 m.

facts.statement: Plesiopharos moelensis is classified as a basal member of the superfamily Plesiosauroidea.
facts.quote: Plesiopharos moelensis is classified as a basal member of Plesiosauroidea.

facts.statement: Plesiopharos lived during the Sinemurian age in layers of the Coimbra Formation found in Portugal.
facts.quote: Plesiopharos moelensis was discovered at Praia da Concha, São Pedro de Moel, Marinha Grande, in layers that belong to the Coimbra Formation, which date to the Sinemurian.

facts.statement: Plesiopharos lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)
